boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Illinois Wesleyan University
boards.description: Ten under-21-safe food stops in Bloomington-Normal with late service documented by current restaurant, ordering, or local-business pages. Confirm same-day hours before leaving campus.

cards.title: The All-Night Drive-Thru
cards.subtitle: Burgers, chicken, chili, and frozen desserts on West Market Street
cards.notes: Check the restaurant locator before departing, then use mobile ordering or the drive-thru for an overnight food run west of campus.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour Bloomington option with a broad fast-food menu and mobile ordering.
cards.evidence_claim: Wendy's official location page identifies the restaurant at 1522 W. Market Street and lists both restaurant and drive-thru service as open 24 hours daily.
cards.source_title: Wendy's 1522 W. Market Street in Bloomington, IL
cards.access_notes: Official locator lists restaurant and drive-thru hours as open 24 hours Monday through Sunday; confirm holiday or temporary changes before travel.

cards.title: Breakfast at Any Hour
cards.subtitle: A round-the-clock diner east of central Bloomington
cards.notes: Use this sit-down option when the group wants breakfast, sandwiches, or dinner food after most kitchens have closed.
cards.short_summary: An all-day diner where breakfast and full meals remain available overnight.
cards.evidence_claim: Denny's official page lists 701 Eldorado Road in Bloomington as open 24 hours every day, with all-day breakfast, lunch, dinner, and walk-in service.
cards.source_title: Denny's Breakfast | 701 Eldorado Rd | Order Online
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists the restaurant as open 24 hours Monday through Sunday; contact the restaurant to confirm holiday hours.

cards.title: The North Main All-Nighter
cards.subtitle: Round-the-clock diner service in neighboring Normal
cards.notes: Choose this northbound diner when a seated meal matters more than proximity, and verify transportation for the return to campus.
cards.short_summary: A second 24-hour diner serving the broader Bloomington-Normal area.
cards.evidence_claim: Denny's official location page identifies 1615 N. Main Street in Normal and lists the restaurant as open 24 hours seven days a week.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists 24-hour service every day, including walk-ins and takeout; confirm holiday hours directly before making the longer trip.

cards.title: The 2 A.M. Drive-Thru
cards.subtitle: Late drive-thru tacos and burritos west of downtown Bloomington
cards.notes: Order ahead and plan on drive-thru access after the dining room closes; the official page separates lobby and drive-thru hours.
cards.short_summary: A nightly drive-thru option that extends two hours beyond midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell's official location page lists the 1702 W. Market Street drive-thru as open until 2:00 a.m. every day and marks the location Open Late.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell in Bloomington, IL — 1702 W. Market St
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru is listed as 9:00 a.m.–2:00 a.m. daily; dine-in closes earlier, so use the drive-thru for service after 10:00 p.m.

cards.title: The 3 A.M. Grill Order
cards.subtitle: Late-night grilled and baked dishes on South Hershey Road
cards.notes: Review the live ordering page before traveling; it displays the restaurant address, menu, and current ordering schedule together.
cards.short_summary: A local grill whose direct ordering page carries service into the early morning.
cards.evidence_claim: Wesley’s Grill's direct Toast ordering page identifies 1804 S. Hershey Road, Suite 10, and lists ordering hours through 3:00 a.m.
cards.source_title: Wesley’s Grill Location and Ordering Hours
cards.access_notes: The direct ordering page lists closing at 3:00 a.m.; consult the live page immediately before ordering because displayed schedules may change.

cards.title: Pizza Until Midnight
cards.subtitle: Long-running neighborhood pizzeria on North Main Street
cards.notes: Place the order well before closing and specify dine-in, carryout, or delivery; Friday and Saturday provide the latest window.
cards.short_summary: A named North Main pizzeria with weekend service reaching midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: Tobin's official menu identifies its Bloomington restaurant and lists hours until midnight on Friday and Saturday, with earlier closing on other nights.
cards.access_notes: Official menu lists 4:30 p.m.–midnight Friday and Saturday, 4:30–11:00 p.m. Monday–Thursday, and 11:00 a.m.–11:00 p.m. Sunday.

cards.title: The Midnight Pizza Pickup
cards.subtitle: Pizza, sandwiches, and sides on East College Avenue in Normal
cards.notes: Check the location page for the live closing time, order online, and allow enough travel time from campus before midnight.
cards.short_summary: A Normal carryout and delivery shop documented as serving until midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: Domino's official location page identifies the store at 1910 E. College Avenue in Normal and displays a closing time of midnight.
cards.source_title: Domino's Pizza at 1910 East College Ave in Normal
cards.access_notes: Official location page displayed service until 12:00 a.m. when fetched; recheck the live page because daily and holiday schedules may vary.

cards.title: Cookies After Midnight
cards.subtitle: Late-night bakery counter on East Beaufort Street
cards.notes: Use the current listing to compare weekday and weekend closing times, then order for pickup or delivery before the posted cutoff.
cards.short_summary: A dessert-focused stop with service extending past midnight on multiple nights.
cards.evidence_claim: Eat Local Bloomington-Normal's current business page identifies Insomnia Cookies at 117 E. Beaufort Street and lists closing at 1:00 or 3:00 a.m., depending on the night.
cards.access_notes: Listing shows midnight-or-later service nightly: 1:00 a.m. Monday–Wednesday and Sunday, and 3:00 a.m. Thursday–Saturday; verify before ordering.

cards.title: The Calzone Night Shift
cards.subtitle: Late-night calzone counter on East Beaufort Street
cards.notes: Check the direct ordering window before leaving Bloomington, then select pickup or delivery and submit the order ahead of cutoff.
cards.short_summary: A calzone shop with online ordering that continues beyond midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: The direct D.P. Dough ordering page identifies the Normal shop at 121 E. Beaufort Street and lists online ordering through 12:45 a.m.
cards.source_title: D.P. Dough — Normal Pickup and Delivery
cards.access_notes: Direct ordering page lists online ordering from 10:30 a.m. to 12:45 a.m.; confirm the active window before travel or checkout.

cards.title: The 11 P.M. Cutoff
cards.subtitle: Late-evening drive-thru and mobile ordering in east Bloomington
cards.notes: Submit a mobile order before the posted cutoff, or use the drive-thru; do not assume service continues past 11:00 p.m.
cards.short_summary: A predictable late-evening option with an explicitly documented closing time.
cards.evidence_claim: McDonald's official restaurant page identifies 2507 E. Oakland Avenue and lists both lobby and drive-thru hours through 11:00 p.m. daily.
cards.source_title: McDonald's at 2507 E Oakland Ave, Bloomington, IL
cards.access_notes: Official page lists lobby and drive-thru hours as 5:30 a.m.–11:00 p.m. Monday through Sunday; order before the stated cutoff.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Illinois Wesleyan spaces for collaborative work, quiet study, student meetings, informal conversation, campus events, and time outdoors.

cards.title: Build a Group Session Around the Furniture
cards.subtitle: Flexible learning space on the first floor of The Ames Library
cards.notes: Claim a booth or table for small-group work, then use the stadium seating to bring everyone together for reports or discussion.
cards.short_summary: A flexible library workspace with booths, tables, movable boards, displays, and tiered seating for switching between group formats.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Wesleyan identifies the Center for Engaged Learning on the east side of The Ames Library’s first floor and welcomes groups of all sizes; its booths, tables, stadium seating, displays, and whiteboards support several collaborative formats.
cards.source_title: Using the Center for Engaged Learning
cards.access_notes: Some or all of the space may be reserved through 25Live; scheduled use does not stop traffic to nearby library services.

cards.title: Take the Work Outside Without Leaving Ames
cards.subtitle: Elevated garden accessible from the library’s entry level
cards.notes: Bring reading or a small conversation outside, and check the reservation calendar before planning a larger organized gathering.
cards.short_summary: An elevated outdoor library space overlooking the landscaped area south of Ames.
cards.evidence_claim: The university describes the Ames Roof Garden as an elevated outdoor space, accessible from the library’s entry level, that overlooks the park-like setting south of the building.
cards.access_notes: The garden can be reserved for special university events; ordinary access remains subject to library operations and scheduled use.

cards.title: Use the Plaza for Work That Needs an Audience
cards.subtitle: Outdoor event space between McPherson Theatre and The Ames Library
cards.notes: Choose the plaza for a student display or small performance, and arrange a reservation before bringing equipment or programming.
cards.short_summary: A bookable outdoor space suited to visible student displays, performances, and other organized activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Wesleyan locates The Ames Plaza between McPherson Theatre and The Ames Library and says it is available for music performances, student displays, and other activities, with electrical outlets provided.
cards.access_notes: Reserve the plaza through 25Live or Conference Services for organized events; outdoor conditions and scheduled activities may affect use.

cards.title: Settle Into the Lower-Level Soft Seating
cards.subtitle: Open study and gathering area in The Ames Library
cards.notes: Use the tables when materials need to spread out, or take a chair or couch for reading; keep the area suitable for shared use.
cards.short_summary: An open lower-library rotunda combining study tables with chairs and couches.
cards.evidence_claim: The university describes the Ames Lower Level Rotunda as an open area containing study tables, comfortable chairs, and couches; it may also be reserved for non-private events.
cards.access_notes: The area is shared and may be reserved only for non-private events; follow current library access rules and posted expectations.

cards.title: Work Side by Side With Campus Software Ready
cards.subtitle: Computer workspace on the entry level’s west side
cards.notes: Bring a partner when a project needs shared screen work, printing, scanning, statistics software, Adobe tools, or campus GIS software.
cards.short_summary: A 24-computer work area with productivity and specialized software plus nearby printing and scanning equipment.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Wesleyan places the Information Commons on the entry-level west side of The Ames Library and lists 24 computers, room for side-by-side work, and two copiers for printing and scanning.
cards.access_notes: Computers are primarily for academic use by IWU students, faculty, and staff; specialized applications are installed only on designated machines.

cards.title: Make Hansen the Group’s Coordination Point
cards.subtitle: Student-center spaces for meeting, studying, relaxing, and campus programs
cards.notes: Meet near the information desk, use a computer station for a quick print, or reserve an appropriate space well before a planned event.
cards.short_summary: A multipurpose student center connecting informal gathering areas, student organizations, event spaces, services, and dining.
cards.evidence_claim: The university says Hansen Student Center includes areas to relax, study, or meet friends, plus an information desk, computer stations, student-organization offices, event support, bookstore, and Tommy’s dining.
cards.access_notes: Current posted in-session hours are 7:30 a.m.–10 p.m. weekdays and 10 a.m.–10 p.m. weekends; summer hours differ. Reservable spaces use 25Live.

cards.title: Catch Up Between Science Classes
cards.subtitle: Daylit gathering space inside the Center for Natural Sciences
cards.notes: Use the atrium for a brief conversation between classes, while leaving circulation and any scheduled research displays unobstructed.
cards.short_summary: A well-lit science-building atrium documented as a gathering point for students and faculty between classes.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Wesleyan’s Chemistry and Biochemistry department states that the well-lit Center for Natural Sciences atrium draws students and faculty between classes for casual conversations.
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to academic-building access, class schedules, and scheduled events; the university does not describe the atrium as a private study room.

cards.title: Look Beyond the Classroom Doors for Study Space
cards.subtitle: Academic building with flexible teaching and study areas
cards.notes: Use an available study area for coursework between classes, and request formal room use through the university scheduling process.
cards.short_summary: A technology-rich academic building whose flexible layout includes spaces for student study alongside classrooms and seminar rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Wesleyan’s 2026 accreditation draft describes State Farm Hall as a four-level, technology-equipped academic facility with flexible teaching and space arrangements; university materials also identify student study areas there.
cards.source_title: Illinois Wesleyan University Assurance Argument Draft
cards.access_notes: Academic-room requests go through 25Live and require approval by the building scheduler; ordinary access is subject to building operations.

cards.title: Choose the Quad Zone That Fits the Plan
cards.subtitle: Main Quad containing several separately identified outdoor event areas
cards.notes: Match the activity to Commencement Plaza, Joslin Atrium Steps, or McPherson Beach, then submit a space request for organized use.
cards.short_summary: The central quad links three named outdoor gathering zones that student organizations can request for activities.
cards.evidence_claim: The current IWU Registered Student Organization Handbook lists the Eckley Quad, also called the Main Quad, as an outdoor space and identifies Commencement Plaza, Joslin Atrium Steps, and McPherson Beach within it.
cards.access_notes: Registered student organizations must follow university booking and event rules; reservations do not override safety, capacity, or campus-use requirements.

cards.title: Move a Small Gathering Into the Peace Garden
cards.subtitle: Named outdoor campus space available through student-organization scheduling
cards.notes: Pick the garden for a modest outdoor meeting or reflective activity, then check 25Live requirements before organizing a group.
cards.short_summary: A named outdoor setting included among the campus spaces student organizations may request.
cards.evidence_claim: The current IWU Registered Student Organization Handbook explicitly lists the IWU Peace Garden among the outdoor spaces available for registered student-organization use.
cards.access_notes: Organized use is governed by university space-booking policies; confirm approval, weather suitability, and any event requirements in advance.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Free public concerts, galleries, library technology, cycling support, and outdoor activities at Illinois Wesleyan University and around Bloomington-Normal.

cards.title: Browse the Merwin Gallery
cards.subtitle: Free contemporary-art exhibitions at Illinois Wesleyan
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition schedule, then meet inside the Ames School of Art and Design for an unhurried gallery walk.
cards.short_summary: See rotating contemporary artwork in the larger of IWU’s two public galleries.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Wesleyan states that all Merwin and Wakeley gallery exhibitions are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Open to the public during posted gallery hours; confirm the exhibition schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Explore the Wakeley Gallery
cards.subtitle: A smaller free exhibition space inside the Ames School
cards.notes: Pair up to examine the smaller-format exhibition closely, leaving time afterward to compare observations outside the gallery.
cards.short_summary: Use the intimate gallery setting for a focused art-looking session with a friend.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Wesleyan identifies Wakeley Gallery as one of its two gallery spaces and states that all exhibitions are free and public.
cards.access_notes: Open to the public during posted gallery hours; exhibitions rotate, so consult the gallery page first.

cards.title: Hear the Honor Orchestra
cards.subtitle: A free School of Music event in Bloomington
cards.notes: Bring a classmate to the scheduled performance and arrive early enough to settle in before the ensemble begins playing.
cards.short_summary: Share a live orchestral performance without buying admission.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU lists Honor Orchestra among its 2026 annual music highlights and says all School of Music events are public and free of charge.
cards.access_notes: Open to the public and free of charge; confirm the event time and venue with the Music Office because programs may change.

cards.title: Listen at Titan Choral Fest
cards.subtitle: Free choral programming from the IWU School of Music
cards.notes: Invite friends who enjoy vocal music, verify the calendar listing, and gather at the announced venue before the program starts.
cards.short_summary: Make a no-cost group outing around live choral music.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU lists Titan Choral Fest as a 2026 annual highlight and states that every School of Music event is open publicly and free of charge.
cards.access_notes: Public and free of charge; check the live calendar or contact the Music Office to confirm scheduling and location.

cards.title: Catch the Honor Band
cards.subtitle: A free ensemble event on the School of Music calendar
cards.notes: Choose a meeting point near Presser Hall, confirm the final venue, and enjoy the student musicians’ program together.
cards.short_summary: Turn a scheduled band performance into a free campus meetup.
cards.evidence_claim: The university’s music calendar lists Honor Band for 2026 and declares all School of Music events open to the public and free of charge.
cards.access_notes: No admission charge and public access; programs can change, so verify the performance details before going.

cards.title: Meet Up for Honor Jazz Band
cards.subtitle: Free jazz programming at Illinois Wesleyan
cards.notes: Check the School of Music calendar near the event date, then meet at the confirmed campus venue for the performance.
cards.short_summary: Hear young jazz musicians perform during a free public program.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU names Honor Jazz Band among its 2026 annual highlights and says all School of Music events are open to the public for free.
cards.access_notes: Open to the public with no charge; verify the current time and venue because the university notes that programs may change.

cards.title: Drop In on the Jazz Festival
cards.subtitle: Free daytime performances and clinics at Westbrook Auditorium
cards.notes: Use the published festival schedule to select a performance block at Westbrook Auditorium and coordinate arrival with friends.
cards.short_summary: Sample several jazz performances during IWU’s annual campus festival.
cards.evidence_claim: The official 2026 Jazz Festival program identifies Westbrook Auditorium as the venue and states that admission is free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: 51st Annual Illinois Wesleyan Jazz Festival Program
cards.access_notes: The campus festival program is free and public; use the current calendar for the next edition and exclude separately priced off-campus encores.

cards.title: Hold a Library Computer Session
cards.subtitle: No-charge computers at Bloomington Public Library
cards.notes: Bring a valid library card or eCard, claim neighboring computers if available, and work through a shared research task.
cards.short_summary: Use the library’s computers for a collaborative digital work session.
cards.evidence_claim: Bloomington Public Library says its Wi-Fi, desktop computers, and laptops may be used without charge; computers require a valid card or eCard.
cards.access_notes: Computer use requires a valid library card or eCard; building hours and available devices can vary.

cards.entity_name: Hansen Student Center Bike Repair Station
cards.title: Tune Up Bikes at Hansen
cards.subtitle: A free repair station on the IWU campus
cards.notes: Bring a bicycle needing a small adjustment and use the station’s basic tools together before taking a short test ride.
cards.short_summary: Handle basic bicycle maintenance with the free tools outside Hansen Student Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town of Normal lists a free bicycle-repair station at Illinois Wesleyan’s Hansen Student Center, 300 E. Beecher Street.
cards.access_notes: The station supplies basic tools and is free to use; bring any replacement parts your bicycle requires.

cards.title: Walk Through Refuge Food Forest
cards.subtitle: Free public produce at One Normal Plaza
cards.notes: Visit with a friend, identify what is ready to harvest, and pick only usable produce while leaving enough for others.
cards.short_summary: Combine an outdoor walk with responsible harvesting from a public food forest.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town of Normal states that Refuge Food Forest is open to the public and that its produce is free to pick.
cards.access_notes: Public access and produce picking are free; harvest only available produce and observe posted site guidance.

warnings: The School of Music states that programs are subject to change; confirm dates, times, and venues before attending.
The 2026 Jazz Festival has concluded as of the fetch date; consult the official calendar for the next annual edition.
Coordinates were left null because exact point coordinates were not established by the cited direct sources.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct Illinois Wesleyan study settings, from reservable project rooms and technology-equipped work areas to quiet floors and an outdoor roof garden.

cards.title: Spread Out in the CEL
cards.subtitle: Flexible first-floor space with booths, tables, screens, and whiteboards
cards.notes: Bring group materials to a booth or study table, then use the movable dry-erase boards; request markers from the front desk if needed.
cards.short_summary: A flexible group-work zone with multiple seating formats and presentation tools.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU identifies the Center for Engaged Learning on the east side of Ames Library’s first floor and documents booths, study tables, stadium seating, displays, and mobile whiteboards.
cards.source_title: Using the Center for Engaged Learning
cards.access_notes: Groups of all sizes are welcome. Individual areas or the entire CEL may be reserved; ordinary traffic continues through the space even during reservations. Follow current Ames Library hours.

cards.title: Build a Research Base at the Information Commons
cards.subtitle: Entry-level computer area beside library help
cards.notes: Choose this area when assignments need campus software, printing, or scanning, and ask the nearby Library Services Desk for research guidance.
cards.short_summary: A 24-computer workspace suited to software-heavy research and side-by-side work.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU states that the entry-level west-side Information Commons has 24 Windows computers, specialized software, room for side-by-side work, and two copiers for printing and scanning.
cards.access_notes: Library computers are primarily for academic use by IWU students, faculty, and staff. Access follows current Ames Library hours.

cards.title: Put the Screen to Work in Room 130
cards.subtitle: Reservable project room with computer, webcam, monitor, and DVD player
cards.notes: Reserve this room for a small collaborative session that needs a shared screen or DVD playback, and submit the booking at least 24 hours ahead.
cards.short_summary: A reservable media-ready room for structured group assignments and presentations.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU lists Project Room 130 among three reservable Ames Library rooms equipped with a computer, webcam, and large monitor; Room 130 also has a DVD player.
cards.access_notes: IWU patrons must reserve the room at least 24 hours ahead in 60-minute increments. The daily limit is four hours, with bookings accepted up to one month ahead.

cards.title: Rehearse Together in Room 134
cards.subtitle: Reservable collaboration room with computer, webcam, and large monitor
cards.notes: Book Room 134 for a team draft review or presentation rehearsal, then confirm the listed seating capacity in the reservation system.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated room where a group can collaborate around one shared display.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU identifies Project Room 134 as a reservable Ames Library room equipped with a computer, webcam, and large-screen monitor.
cards.access_notes: IWU patrons must reserve the room at least 24 hours ahead in 60-minute increments. Check the reservation site for current seating capacity.

cards.title: Move the Meeting Upstairs to Room 214
cards.subtitle: Second-floor reservable room with collaborative technology
cards.notes: Use Room 214 when a discussion needs privacy and a common display; schedule the session early enough to meet the advance-booking rule.
cards.short_summary: An upstairs project room designed for focused, technology-supported teamwork.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU lists Room 214 as one of three reservable Ames Library project rooms and says it includes a computer, webcam, and large-screen monitor.
cards.access_notes: IWU patrons must reserve the room at least 24 hours ahead in 60-minute increments. Reservations are limited to four hours per day.

cards.title: Settle Into the Lower Level Rotunda
cards.subtitle: Open study area with tables, comfortable chairs, and couches
cards.notes: Pick a table for materials or a softer chair for reading, but check posted notices because the open rotunda can also be reserved for events.
cards.short_summary: An open lower-level setting that supports both tabletop work and informal reading.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU describes the Lower Level Rotunda as an open Ames Library area furnished with study tables, comfortable chairs, and couches.
cards.access_notes: This is a non-private area and may be reserved for events. Follow posted notices and current Ames Library building hours.

cards.title: Lower the Volume on Floor Three
cards.subtitle: Designated quiet floor with reading space and scholarly workstations
cards.notes: Bring headphones and keep conversation low; choose a scholarly workstation when the assignment needs office, statistics, or research software.
cards.short_summary: A quiet-floor option combining individual reading space with academic computers.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU designates the third floor as a quiet floor and documents four scholarly workstations on its west side with office and academic software.
cards.access_notes: Maintain a low volume and follow posted signage. Community computer access is permitted, but printing is unavailable to community members; building hours apply.

cards.title: Take Deep Work to Floor Four
cards.subtitle: Designated quiet floor with naturally lit reading areas
cards.notes: Use this floor for low-volume individual work, and keep clear of Tate Archives materials unless you are working within its separate access guidelines.
cards.short_summary: A quiet upper-floor environment for concentrated reading and writing.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU identifies the fourth floor as a quiet floor, while its library history page describes quiet reading spaces with abundant natural light throughout Ames Library.
cards.access_notes: Maintain a low volume and follow posted signage. Tate Archives on the fourth floor has separate weekday hours and collection-use guidelines.

cards.title: Take the Reading Outside at the Roof Garden
cards.subtitle: Elevated outdoor space overlooking the library’s south-side landscape
cards.notes: Bring portable reading or a short discussion outside in suitable weather, and verify that the garden is not reserved for a university event.
cards.short_summary: An elevated open-air alternative for weather-friendly reading and conversation.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU describes the Ames Roof Garden as an elevated outdoor space accessible from the entry level and overlooking a park-like setting south of the library.
cards.access_notes: Access is from the library entry level and depends on building access, weather, and event reservations. The garden may be reserved for special university events.

cards.title: Find a Floor That Fits at State Farm Hall
cards.subtitle: Study areas distributed through a four-floor academic building
cards.notes: Walk the floors to select an available study area that fits solo or collaborative work, while yielding scheduled instructional rooms to classes.
cards.short_summary: Multiple study areas inside a technology-rich academic and collaborative building.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU reports that State Farm Hall is a four-floor academic and collaborative facility with study spaces on each floor used by students from varied majors.
cards.source_title: IWU Celebrates a Decade of Business, Economics, Finance Education at State Farm Hall
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to current academic-building access and scheduled classes or events; the cited page does not publish general building hours or reservation rules.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on streets and corridors in Illinois Wesleyan’s practical Bloomington orbit, each paired with one verified reason to go.

cards.title: Coffee on the 400 Block
cards.subtitle: North Main Street corridor
cards.notes: Follow North Main Street downtown for a café stop; check the official location page before setting out for current daily hours.
cards.short_summary: A downtown café anchors this walk along Main Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Coffee Hound operates its Downtown Bloomington café at 407 N. Main Street and lists daily hours of 6:30 a.m.–4 p.m.
cards.access_notes: The official location page lists daily hours of 6:30 a.m.–4 p.m.; purchases are required for café items.

cards.title: Browse a Local Bookshop
cards.subtitle: North Main Street corridor
cards.notes: Continue to the 400 block of North Main Street and browse the shop’s new, used, and out-of-print books or literary gifts.
cards.short_summary: An independent bookstore gives North Main Street a browsing stop.
cards.evidence_claim: Bobzbay Books is located at 419 N. Main Street and sells new, used, and out-of-print books.
cards.access_notes: Retail bookstore; confirm current storefront hours before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Bloomington Center for the Performing Arts
cards.title: Find the Downtown Stage
cards.subtitle: North East Street corridor
cards.notes: Walk the North East Street corridor to see the performing-arts center’s exterior, then consult its schedule for a ticketed event.
cards.short_summary: A civic performance venue marks the cultural end of East Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Bloomington facility directory lists Bloomington Center for the Performing Arts at 600 N. East Street.
cards.source_title: Facility Directory Formatted List | Bloomington, IL Parks & Recreation
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing does not require entry; event access and ticket requirements vary by performance.

cards.title: Enter Through Washington Street
cards.subtitle: Downtown Main Street corridor
cards.notes: Circle the courthouse square, then use the museum entrance on Washington Street to explore seven galleries and local-history collections.
cards.short_summary: The former courthouse turns the Main Street square into a history stop.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum occupies 200 N. Main Street, has its public entrance on Washington Street, and contains seven exhibit galleries.
cards.source_title: Visit | McLean County Museum of History
cards.access_notes: Open Monday–Saturday with varying hours; students and children receive free admission according to the museum.

cards.title: Use the Library’s Evening Window
cards.subtitle: East Olive Street corridor
cards.notes: Head along East Olive Street for reading, research, or study; Monday through Thursday hours extend into the evening.
cards.short_summary: The city library provides an indoor destination on Olive Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Bloomington Public Library is located at 205 E. Olive Street and lists 9 a.m.–9 p.m. hours Monday through Thursday.
cards.source_title: Bloomington Public Library | Bloomington Public Library
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are Mon–Thu 9 a.m.–9 p.m., Fri–Sat 9 a.m.–5 p.m., and Sun 1–5 p.m.; check holiday closures.

cards.title: Check the Arena Marquee
cards.subtitle: South Madison Street corridor
cards.notes: Walk South Madison Street to inspect the arena marquee and exterior; use the official calendar before planning entry for an event.
cards.short_summary: A large civic arena defines this downtown Madison Street block.
cards.evidence_claim: Grossinger Motors Arena lists its location as 101 South Madison Street and notes an attached parking deck plus nearby public parking.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Grossinger Motors Arena
cards.access_notes: Public entry depends on the scheduled event; consult the official event listing for age rules, tickets, and door times.

cards.title: Pause at a Lighted Park Walkway
cards.subtitle: Bell Street and Emerson Street corridor
cards.notes: Approach from the Emerson Street corridor, use the park’s main walkway, and pause at the picnic tables during a daytime circuit.
cards.short_summary: A compact neighborhood park adds a green pause near Emerson Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Bloomington Parks lists Emerson Park at 717 Bell Street as a 2.4-acre park with picnic tables, playground equipment, and a lighted main walkway.
cards.source_title: Emerson Park | Bloomington, IL Parks & Recreation
cards.access_notes: Municipal park; use during posted park hours and follow on-site rules.

cards.title: Swim on West Chestnut
cards.subtitle: West Chestnut Street corridor
cards.notes: Take West Chestnut Street to the seasonal aquatic center; review the current schedule and admission details before bringing swim gear.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal pool complex supplies the active option on Chestnut Street.
cards.evidence_claim: O'Neil Aquatics Center is located in O'Neil Park at 1515 W. Chestnut Street and includes leisure and lap pools, slides, and a lazy river.
cards.source_title: O'Neil Aquatics Center | Bloomington, IL Parks & Recreation
cards.access_notes: Seasonal facility; consult the current pool schedule, weather notices, rules, and admission information before traveling.

cards.title: Follow Morris Avenue to the Zoo
cards.subtitle: South Morris Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Use South Morris Avenue to reach the zoo, then choose among indoor and outdoor habitats after checking the day’s operating notices.
cards.short_summary: Animal habitats provide a clearly marked destination on Morris Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: Miller Park Zoo is at 1020 S. Morris Avenue and features indoor and outdoor habitats including Tropical America Rainforest and Wallaby WalkAbout.
cards.source_title: Meet Your Zoo Friends! | Bloomington, IL Parks & Recreation
cards.access_notes: The zoo lists daily hours of 9:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m., with grounds cleared at 5 p.m.; admission is required.

cards.title: End at Clover Lawn
cards.subtitle: Monroe Drive corridor
cards.notes: Follow Monroe Drive to the mansion grounds and visitor center; arrive before the final scheduled tour and review accessibility details.
cards.short_summary: A state historic mansion gives Monroe Drive an architectural endpoint.
cards.evidence_claim: The David Davis Mansion at 1000 Monroe Drive is a 36-room late-Victorian house with surviving estate structures and an ornamental garden.
cards.source_title: David Davis Mansion | Illinois Department of Natural Resources
cards.access_notes: The state lists Wednesday–Saturday hours of 9 a.m.–3:30 p.m.; check the current tour schedule before visiting.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Illinois Wesleyan rituals and recurring events, from pineapple pats and fountain chalking to finals-week food and fall-semester gatherings.

cards.title: Write a Goal, Then Find Your Name
cards.subtitle: A four-year chalk cycle around Aspiration Fountain
cards.notes: During Turning Titan, chalk a college goal by the fountain; before Commencement, return to see faculty and staff honor graduates by name.
cards.short_summary: First-year ambitions and graduating-class names temporarily transform the same campus pavement.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Wesleyan states that first-year students chalk college goals around Aspiration Fountain during orientation and that faculty and staff later chalk graduates’ names there before Commencement.
cards.access_notes: The first-year activity occurs during Turning Titan; the graduate-name display is installed in the lead-up to Commencement.

cards.title: Pat the Pineapple on the Way Out
cards.subtitle: A stone symbol marks the passage from student to alumnus
cards.notes: Watch for the stone pineapple at Commencement and give it the customary pat while crossing the stage into the alumni community.
cards.short_summary: Graduates complete their Illinois Wesleyan passage with an unexpectedly tropical stone landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Wesleyan documents that seniors pat a stone pineapple while crossing the Commencement stage, symbolizing their transition into the Titan alumni community.
cards.access_notes: Participation is tied to the University’s Commencement ceremony and its graduating seniors.

cards.title: Let the President Serve Breakfast
cards.subtitle: Finals Week turns pancakes into an evening ritual
cards.notes: Take a finals study break for pancakes, eggs, sausage and tots served by the University president and other administrators.
cards.short_summary: Administrators swap official duties for breakfast service during the fall examination rush.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Wesleyan identifies Late Night Breakfast as an annual fall Finals Week tradition featuring breakfast food served to students by the president and other administrators.
cards.access_notes: Held late at night during fall-semester Finals Week; the public traditions page does not provide the next event’s exact time or venue.

cards.title: Pause Finals for a PB&J
cards.subtitle: A second late-night Finals Week food custom
cards.notes: Step away from studying for a peanut-butter-and-jelly sandwich and snacks when the campus stages its Finals Week PB&J Night.
cards.short_summary: The familiar packed-lunch sandwich becomes a named nighttime examination-week tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Wesleyan describes PB&J Night as a Finals Week tradition where students take a late-night study break for peanut-butter-and-jelly sandwiches and other snacks.
cards.access_notes: Held late at night during Finals Week; the public traditions page does not list the next date, time or allergen arrangements.

cards.title: End Orientation on a Climbing Wall
cards.subtitle: Turning Titan closes with rides, inflatables and food
cards.notes: Finish fall orientation at the campus carnival; look for rides, a climbing wall, large inflatables and food on the final evening.
cards.short_summary: The orientation finale replaces another meeting with a full-scale outdoor carnival.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Wesleyan says Titan Carnival gathers the campus community on the final evening of fall orientation, with rides, a climbing wall, jumbo inflatables and food.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled for the final evening of Turning Titan; individual attractions may carry their own participation requirements.

cards.title: Meet the Whole Club Roster at Once
cards.subtitle: Registered student organizations take over the Quad
cards.notes: Walk the Quad, speak directly with organization members and note follow-up meetings before choosing where to get involved.
cards.short_summary: Illinois Wesleyan’s registered organizations assemble together for one concentrated introduction.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Wesleyan documents the RSO Fair as a fall tradition where registered student organizations gather to introduce involvement opportunities; its 2026 page schedules the fair for August 26 on the Quad.
cards.access_notes: The published 2026 RSO Involvement Fair is Wednesday, August 26, from 2:30–4:30 p.m. on the Quad.

cards.title: Walk the Campus Red Carpet
cards.subtitle: An annual formal celebration of campus cultures
cards.notes: Register when invitations open, dress for the announced theme and arrive early for student performances before the dancing begins.
cards.short_summary: Students, employees and alumni gather for a red-carpet evening built around cultural expression.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Wesleyan announced its eighth annual Unity Gala for March 7, 2026, featuring cultural performances, food, dancing and celebration at Hansen Student Center, with free registration.
cards.source_title: Upcoming Unity Gala to Celebrate the Cultivation of Community
cards.access_notes: The documented 2026 event has concluded; future dates and registration requirements should be confirmed through the University.

cards.title: Spend Five Days Turning Titan
cards.subtitle: New students begin with a named fall-orientation rite
cards.notes: Plan to attend the full program, meet your first-year adviser and use Titan Orientation Leaders to learn campus resources.
cards.short_summary: Incoming students formally enter campus life through Illinois Wesleyan’s multi-day orientation program.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Wesleyan describes Turning Titan as a multi-day fall program for community-building, advising and resource introductions and lists it as mandatory for first-year and transfer students.
cards.access_notes: The 2026 program runs August 19–23 for new students and August 20–23 for transfer students; no registration is required.

cards.title: Cheer for a Chariot-Born Titan
cards.subtitle: The gladiator mascot carries a campus-specific backstory
cards.notes: Spot Tommy at campus gatherings, then trace the character from a 1951 illustration to the photographed 1965 chariot entrance.
cards.short_summary: Illinois Wesleyan’s named gladiator mascot entered school lore with an actual Roman-style chariot appearance.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Wesleyan credits alumnus Lee Short ’44 with creating Tommy’s gladiator image and name in 1951 and records Tommy’s 1965 football pregame entrance in a Roman-style chariot.
cards.access_notes: Mascot appearances vary by event; consult the relevant University or athletics schedule before planning a visit.

cards.title: Sing “Alma Wesleyana”
cards.subtitle: A school song preserved in the Titan songbook
cards.notes: Learn the brief alma mater from the University songbook and listen to the official Wind Ensemble arrangement before a campus ceremony.
cards.short_summary: The school’s ceremonial affection is expressed through a compact, century-spanning alma mater.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Wesleyan’s official traditions page publishes the words to “Alma Wesleyana” and provides an official songbook recording arranged by alumnus Peter Gilbert ’98.
cards.access_notes: The lyrics and recordings are publicly available; live performance depends on the ceremony or campus event.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Illinois Wesleyan University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A practical, under-21-safe sequence for learning the campus, finding student resources, and exploring two public Bloomington destinations.

cards.title: Start at the student center
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Get oriented
cards.notes: Locate the information desk, Student Involvement office, bookstore, and Tommy’s so you know where to return for help and events.
cards.short_summary: Use Hansen as your first reference point for campus services and involvement.
cards.evidence_claim: Hansen Student Center houses an information desk, bookstore, Tommy’s dining, Student Involvement, student organizations, and meeting spaces.
cards.access_notes: During fall and spring classes, the building lists Friday hours of 7:30 a.m.–10 p.m. and weekend hours of 10 a.m.–10 p.m.; summer weekends are closed.

cards.title: Learn the center of campus
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Walk the main quad
cards.notes: Cross Eckley Quadrangle and identify the surrounding landmarks now; it will make later walks between campus buildings easier.
cards.short_summary: Build a mental map by walking IWU’s named main quadrangle.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU’s current campus map names Eckley Quadrangle, and the student-organization handbook identifies it as the Main Quad.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus location; check campus notices and posted restrictions before visiting.

cards.title: Set up your study anchor
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Find academic support
cards.notes: Step inside, locate the service desk, and note where the Writing Center, technology help, and other learning-support units are based.
cards.short_summary: Find the library services and campus partners you may need once classes begin.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ames Library provides research services and houses the Writing Center, Information Technology Services, and other student-support units.
cards.source_title: The Ames Library – Faculty & Staff Directory
cards.access_notes: Regular fall and spring hours are Friday 7:45 a.m.–5 p.m., Saturday 10 a.m.–4 p.m., and Sunday noon–8 p.m.; orientation and break schedules differ.

cards.title: Make an art stop
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · See the current exhibition
cards.notes: Enter through the Ames School of Art and Design, check the posted exhibition information, and spend a focused half hour with the work.
cards.short_summary: Add a free contemporary-art visit to your first campus circuit.
cards.evidence_claim: The Merwin and Wakeley Galleries present contemporary art exhibitions and state that exhibitions are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are Monday–Friday noon–4 p.m., Tuesday 7–9 p.m., and Saturday–Sunday 1–4 p.m.; verify the current exhibition calendar.

cards.title: Pause downtown
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · Choose your own order
cards.notes: Use the official menu or ordering app if you want something, then orient yourself on North Main Street before continuing downtown.
cards.short_summary: Begin Saturday at a named all-ages café in Downtown Bloomington.
cards.evidence_claim: The Coffee Hound’s official locations page lists its Downtown Bloomington café at 407 N. Main Street and daily hours of 6:30 a.m.–4 p.m.
cards.access_notes: The business currently lists daily hours of 6:30 a.m.–4 p.m.; confirm before departing because business hours can change.

cards.title: Meet Bloomington through its history
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · Explore the courthouse museum
cards.notes: Enter from Washington Street and choose one of the permanent galleries as your starting point rather than trying to cover all four floors.
cards.short_summary: Connect your new campus town to the people and events preserved by its history museum.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum occupies four floors, offers five permanent exhibits and a Discovery Room, and grants free admission to students and children.
cards.access_notes: The museum lists Saturday hours of 9 a.m.–5 p.m. and directs visitors to its Washington Street entrance at 200 N. Main Street.

cards.title: Return for a garden reset
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Walk a campus growing space
cards.notes: Follow the campus map to the Peace Garden, observe what is growing, and leave beds and greenhouse areas undisturbed unless invited to help.
cards.short_summary: See how a named campus garden connects food, learning, and civic engagement.
cards.evidence_claim: The IWU Peace Garden serves students’ curricular and culinary needs and supports civic engagement and food-growing partnerships.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor garden conditions and organized work opportunities vary; follow posted guidance and do not enter restricted growing areas.

cards.title: Find the recreation hub
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Scope out future workouts
cards.notes: Walk through only where student access permits, note the recreation and fitness areas, and check posted schedules before planning a workout.
cards.short_summary: Learn where IWU students go for indoor recreation, fitness, and athletics.
cards.evidence_claim: The Shirk Center is used by students for fitness and recreation and includes multi-use courts, a 200-meter track, and fitness facilities.
cards.source_title: IWU’s Shirk Center Celebrating 30 Years of Athletics, Community
cards.access_notes: Student entry and facility availability depend on identification requirements, posted schedules, team use, and events; verify before exercising.

cards.title: Take a daylight trail walk
cards.subtitle: Sunday morning · Explore a short segment
cards.notes: Choose a signed trailhead, keep right, stay aware at crossings, and turn back while you still have ample daylight for the return trip.
cards.short_summary: Use a manageable walk to see part of Bloomington-Normal beyond campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Constitution Trail is a public multi-segment trail system connecting Bloomington and Normal, with mapped trailheads and recreation rules.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from one hour before sunrise until one hour after sunset. Keep right, obey signs, and use designated access points and crossings.

cards.title: Close with a quiet check-in
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · Study, reflect, or talk
cards.notes: Visit the open common spaces for a brief reset, and note the Multifaith Engagement office as a resource for future questions or programs.
cards.short_summary: End the weekend in an inclusive campus space for reflection and conversation.
cards.evidence_claim: Evelyn Chapel houses the Office of Multifaith Engagement and provides spaces to study, converse, and prepare complimentary hot drinks.
cards.access_notes: The university currently states that Evelyn Chapel is open seven days a week from 8 a.m.–11 p.m.; scheduled programs may affect individual spaces.

warnings: Business, facility, exhibition, and academic-calendar hours can change; consult the linked direct pages and posted notices before visiting.
Coordinates and map URLs are null because they were not independently verified from direct authoritative pages during this pass.
